extracted.intended_audience: early-modern chymists and experimental natural philosophers (practitioners of distillation and compound analysis)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and experimental protocols for judging claims about elemental ingredients (water, earth, salts) in mixt bodies and for preparing/separating volatile salts; combines epistemic criteria with practical distillation/flux procedures. Useful for assessing whether observed products indicate true elementary constituents or are artefacts of operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for calling a substance 'water' (phlegme)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief Qualities which make men give that name to any visible Substance, are, that it is Fluid or Liquid, and that it is insipid and inodorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on a single apparent quality: the text examines how distillation yields liquors judged 'phlegme' by taste/smell but questions equating insipidity with elementary water. Examples given (sea-salt spirits, spirit of quicksilver) show distinct liquids can be tasteless; therefore identification as 'water' requires further corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fluidity by particle size and motion
rubrics_metrics.description: To a Body's being Fluid there is nothing necessary, but that it be divided into parts small enough; and that these parts be put into such a motion among themselves as to glide some this way and some that way, along each other's Surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging whether a product is a 'liquid' or 'water', consider microstructure: comminution into sufficiently small mobile corpuscles can produce fluid behaviour even absent an elementary aqueous ingredient. Experimental designs should consider particle-size effects produced by fire or other agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not infer elemental ingredients solely from distillation products
rubrics_metrics.description: Dry Bodies may by the Fire be reduc'd to Liquors without any separation of Elements, but barely by a certain kind of Dissipation and Comminution of the matter, whereby its parts are brought into a new state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observing a liquor upon distillation does not prove that water (or any supposed element) pre-existed in the mixture; experimentalists must rule out that liquefaction arose from change of texture/size of corpuscles rather than liberation of an elemental ingredient. Many examples provided (sea-salt yielding liquor, quicksilver transforms) illustrate this anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insipidity/inodorousness alone not proof of 'elementary' water
rubrics_metrics.description: Helmont pronounc'd it so, then that it is insipid. Sapour being an Accident ... it may very possibly be, that the small Parts of a Body may be of such a Size and Shape ... to be unable to pierce ... the Organs of Tast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensory absence (taste/smell) can result from particle size/shape or association effects; therefore do not identify a liquor as elemental water merely because it is tasteless or odourless. Use additional physical and chemical tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hasty dismissal of residues as 'earth' or 'useless fæces'
rubrics_metrics.description: I have taken notice of the unwarrantable forwardness of common Chymists to pronounce things useless Fæces, by observing how often they reject the Caput Mortuum of Verdegrease; which is yet so farr from deserving that Name, that not only by strong fires and convenient Additaments it may in some hours be reduc'd into copper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before declaring a distillation residue to be inert 'earth', subject it to further skilled examination (strong fires, flux powders, specific reagents). Historical examples (Agricola's Regulus from sulphur fæces; recovering copper from verdegrease residues) show valuable metals or different substances can lurk in dismissed residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different resolving agents and operations give different decompositions
rubrics_metrics.description: I see not why it should be necessary that all Agents that resolve Bodies into portions of differingly qualifi'd matter must work on them the same way... some Tools reduce Wood ... Files and Saws makes a Comminution of it into Dust ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating composition, test a variety of agents (fire, spirit of wine, aqua fortis, mechanical comminution, churning, rennet, etc.) because distinct agents produce distinct separations and products. Do not generalize from one method's result to all ways matter can be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: To claim a primary/indestructible element requires showing permanence under varied operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Though those I dispute with are not yet able out of Gold, or Silver, or divers other Concretes to separate any thing like Water; I hope I may be allow'd to conclude ... that water it self is not an Universal and pre-existent Ingredient of Mixt Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A putative element should be shown to resist destruction or further reduction by a wide range of agents. The burden of proof is to demonstrate that no conceivable operation yields different constituents; absence of evidence from a limited set of operations is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider particle figure, size, and association as explanations for altered properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corpuscles into which a body is dissipated by the Fire may ... have their figures so altered, or may be by associations with one another brought into little Masses of such a Size and Shape, as not to be fit to make sensible Impressions on the Tongue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for morphological and associative changes at the microscopic/corpuscular level when interpreting loss or change of sensory properties. Experimental interpretation must separate true chemical/compositional change from textural/structural effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple reactivity and physical tests before asserting identity
rubrics_metrics.description: This Spirit abounds in the Salt I told you of ... it hisses upon the Affusion of Spirit of Nitre, or Oyle of Vitriol; it precipitates Corals Dissolv'd in Spirit of Vinager; it turnes the blew Syrup of Violets immediately green; it presentlie turnes the Solution of Sublimate into a Milkie whiteness ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify new salts or bodies by a battery of characteristic reactions (acid interaction, precipitation of known substances, colorimetric changes, effects on other solutions). Relying on a single observation (e.g., taste) is inadequate; document multiple diagnostic behaviours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for producing a volatile salt ('Tartari Fugitivus')
rubrics_metrics.description: Take then of good Antimony, Salt-Petre and Tartar, of each an equal weight, and of Quicklime Halfe the Weight of any one of them; ... cast in the Mixture ... the Fumes will pass into the Receiver and condense there into a Liquor, that being rectifi'd will be of a pure golden Colour ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, stepwise protocol: powder and mix reagents in specified proportions; use a long-necked earthen retort in a furnace with a receiver; heat until red hot and feed small quantities through the top hole; collect and rectify the condensed spirit. This is offered as a reproducible experimental recipe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation by sublimation using a glass egg in hot sand
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of which may easily enough be separated ... to put the Liquor into a glass Egg, or bolthead with a long and narrow Neck. For if this be plac'd a little inclining in hot sand, there will sublime up a fine Salt ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To isolate the volatile salt from the rectified spirit, employ a glass vessel with a long neck inclined in hot sand to promote sublimation and deposition of crystalline salt. This is a recommended laboratory technique for separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report multiple observable qualities (taste, smell, colour, sublimability, reactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Salt I speak of falls extreamly short of those Virtues ... not seeming in its Tast, Smel, and other Obvious Qualities, to differ very much ... Nor have I yet made Tryals enough to be sure ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before asserting the nature or virtues of a preparation, accumulate and describe sensory and chemical data (taste, smell, appearance, reactions). Note uncertainty and avoid overclaiming when trials are insufficient; replication and further trials are warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider natural generation and transformation when attributing source to product
rubrics_metrics.description: I produced divers other Vegetables of very differing Natures out of Water ... it may likewise receive its Nutriment from the water attracted out of the earth ... the same Liquor being Digested in the plant, ... is turn'd into the Wood, Bark, Pith, Leaves, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that the presence of an element in an organism implies that element pre-existed as a discrete ingredient; consider that biological and natural formative powers can transmute simple fluids into diverse substances (plants, salts, charcoal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish dissolution in a menstruum from destructive decomposition by fire
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherefore if you dissolve the purer sort of Vitriol in common Water, the Liquor will swallow up the Mineral ... yet each of these Corpuscles retains its Nature and Texture, and remains a Vitriolate and Compounded Body. But if the same Vitriol be exposed to a strong Fire, it will then be divided not only ... into Heterogeneous Substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret analytical outcomes in light of method: solvation can give the appearance of incorporation without destroying prior corpuscular texture, whereas calcination may produce genuinely new heterogeneous substances. Choose analytical method according to the ontological claim being tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental humility: require skilful, repeated, and varied trials before strong claims
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a great Disparity betwixt the Operations of the several Agents whereby the Parts of a Body come to be Dissipated ... I have divers times separated a salt from Oyle of Vitriol ... I have not yet made Tryals enough to be sure ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid strong universal inferences from limited or vulgar trials. Skilled manipulation and repeated/cohobated operations can yield different products; acknowledge limits, repeat experiments, and use careful technique before promulgating broad theoretical conclusions.
